subject: Re: Order Form - tier phasing, surge protection and fair-use language
messages:
From: Amrita Singh <amrita@cloudshift.com>

Cc: Ravi Patel <ravi@cloudshift.com>, CloudShift Legal <legal@cloudshift.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 08:34:12 -0700
Subject: Order Form Sched C - initial redlines

Mina — thanks for the walkthrough earlier. Attached is CloudShift's redline of Schedule C (pricing schedule) and a short note on the ramp assumptions. High level asks from procurement/legal: 

- Add a firm fair-use surge cap (we propose a 2x cap on sustained monthly overage beyond committed tiers) so our cost exposure during spikes is bounded.
- Phase-in tiered pricing over the first three quarters to account for initial onboarding variability (Q1 50% of target, Q2 80%, Q3 full).
- Remove unilateral fee floor increases and replace with a mutual review/notice process tied to usage regressions.
- Add explicit credit carryover for unused committed tokens in migration months.

We included suggested language in the attached CloudShift_Redline_SchedC.docx and marked the most sensitive clauses. We'd like to get to a negotiation call by Friday.

Thanks,
Amrita
Director, Strategic Sourcing
CloudShift Inc.

Mina / team — reviewed CloudShift's redline. High-level legal position and suggested compromise language below (I tracked key points only):

1) Surge cap: CloudShift wants a 2x cap on "sustained monthly overage". We can accept a bounded surge but need objective thresholds and tail protection for bursty traffic. Proposed language: "For any calendar month, charges for overage usage above the committed tier shall be capped at 2x the per-token overage rate provided that the overage period exceeds 72 continuous hours; isolated spikes under 72 hours are billed at standard overage rates."

2) Tier phasing: Accept phased effective pricing if commitments are time-boxed and not permanent. Proposed: "Customer commit to target token volume by the end of Q3; phased discounts applied in Q1 and Q2 as set forth in Exhibit C. Any shortfall after Q3 triggers standard true-up mechanics."

3) Fee floor adjustments: We push back on full mutual veto language. Compromise: 60-day notice plus one mutual review call; if no agreement, parties escalate to senior commercial contacts with temporary hold on billing adjustments for 90 days.

4) Carryover credits: Recommend quarter-limited carryover (unused committed tokens may be carried into the following calendar quarter, capped at 25% of the next quarter's committed volume). Unlimited carryover materially changes economics.

I've drafted RI_proposed_language_v1.docx with concrete text. Ben / Laura — please run the model with these constraints and call out P&L impact.

Karthik
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments: RI_proposed_language_v1.docx
From: CloudShift Legal <legal@cloudshift.com>

Date: Fri, 23 Oct 2026 11:22:46 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form Sched C - initial redlines

Mina / Karthik — thanks for the quick turn. A few points from our side after reviewing Karthik's draft:

- The 72-hour sustained threshold is sensible, but CloudShift prefers a 48-hour threshold to capture multi-day outages that are still short in commercial terms. We propose 48 hours.
- We can accept quarter-limited carryover but ask that the cap be 33% of the following quarter's committed volume (instead of 25%). This helps us smooth usage without taking on long-term rollover liability.
- On notice and escalation: we can agree to a 60-day notice and a senior escalations path, but we need a guaranteed temporary credit if a unilateral fee increase is applied during the notice review (limited to the delta between prior and proposed rates for the first 30 days).

We updated our attachment with tracked changes and proposed alternate wording for the credit provision. Happy to take this on a call — Friday 10/23 at 4pm PT would work for Amrita and me. Is that slot good for Redwood?

Regards,
CloudShift Legal
